Collections.Title: Time-lapse of exoplanet Beta Pictoris d orbiting around its host star
Collections.Description:
This time-lapse video shows the exoplanet Beta Pictoris d orbiting around its host star Beta Pictoris over more than a decade. The planet was discovered with the ERIS instrument on ESO’s Very Large Telescope (VLT). The observations were performed in 2025, and it prompted astronomers to search for the planet in previous archival observations. The planet turned up in data from the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope taken earlier in 2025 and 2023, as well as observations with the SPHERE instrument at the VLT going as far back as 2014.

The star Beta Pictoris hosts two already known additional planets: Beta Pictoris b ––the other bright source at the end of the time-lapse–– and Beta Pictoris c, not seen here as it orbits too close to the star.

The orbits of the three planets are seen almost edge-on from Earth. At the end of this clip, the orbits the three planets are displayed face-on, together with the orbits of Solar System planets for comparison.
Collections.Credit: ESO/B. Sutlieff, M. Bonse et al.
